U.S.-CUBA  RELATIONS 

History  on  fast-forward:  The  day  the  U.S.  and  Cuba  reopened  embassies 

Just  after  midnight  on  July  20th,  the  United  States  and  Cuba  restored  diplomatic  relations 
after  a breach  of  fifty-four  years. 

The  Cuban  Interests  Section  in  Washington,  the  Associated  Press  reported,  marked  the 
occasion  by  "switching  its  Twitter  account  to  say  'embassy',"  while  in  Havana,  "the  U.S. 
Interests  Section  uploaded  a new  profile  pictures  to  its  Facebook  and  Twitter  accounts 
that  says  US  EMBASSY  CUBA." 

Shortly  after  4:30am,  "the  single-star  Cuban  flag  was  added  to  the  array  of  more  than  190 
other  flags  in  the  State  Department's  cavernous  marble  lobby,"  the  Los  Angeles  Times 
reported. 

Across  town  at  10:35am,  the  Cuban  flag  was  hoisted  above  the  building  which  first 
opened  as  Cuba's  embassy  in  1919  . Demonstrators  supporting  the  opening  with  Cuba 

alongside  Cuban  government  opponents  — some  chanting  "Viva  Cuba"  and  Viva  Fidel," 
while  others  called  out  "Free  Cuba,"  USA  Today  said  - raised  their  voices  across  16th 
Street  from  the  Meridian  Hill  mansion  located  in  Washington's  Adams  Morgan 
neighborhood. 

Inside  the  building  that  had  served  as  "The  Cuban  Interests  Section,"  since  1977  , Cuban 

Foreign  Minister  Bruno  Rodriguez  praised  the  "wise  leadership  of  Fidel  Castro,  the 
historic  leader  of  the  Cuban  revolution  whose  ideas  we'll  always  revere,"  and  called  on  the 
U.S.  to  return  Guantanamo  Bay  Naval  Base  and  end  the  trade  embargo  against  Cuba. 

Hours  later,  U.S.  Secretary  of  State  John  Kerry  received  Cuba's  top  diplomat  for  talks  that 
touched  on  bilateral  cooperation  on  law  enforcement,  counter-narcotics, 
telecommunications,  the  Internet,  human  rights  and  human  trafficking,  as  well  as  the 

10/17/2016 

This  version  of  Total  Mail  Converter  is  not  registered. 

Page  766 

environment,  the  Miami  Herald  reported.  They  emerged  from  their  meeting  and  held  a 
joint  press  conference  at  1:45pm. 

Appearing  with  Minister  Rodriguez,  Secretary  Kerry  hailed  the  thaw  "as  a time  to  start 
repairing  what  has  been  broken,  and  opening  what  for  too  long  has  been  closed."  White 
House  Press  Secretary  Josh  Earnest  issued  a statement  calling  the  embassy  openings  in 
Washington  and  Havana  "another  demonstration  that  we  don't  have  to  be  imprisoned  by 
the  past." 

Attending  the  flag  raising  at  Cuba's  new  embassy,  Sarah  Stephens,  executive  director  of 
the  Center  for  Democracy  in  the  Americas,  said  on  Monday,  "This  is  a historic  day  and  a 
banner  year  for  U.S.  and  Cuban  diplomacy.  We  are  witnessing  the  long  overdue 
opening  of  a new  era  in  which  the  people  of  both  of  our  countries,  our  businesses,  and  our 
governments  can  engage,  do  business,  treat  each  other  with  respect,  and  begin  to  live 
more  nonnal  lives." 

Cuban  American  lawmakers  denounced  the  diplomatic  developments.  U.S.  Senator  and 
Republican  presidential  hopeful  Marco  Rubio  (FL)  said,  "History  will  remember  July  20, 
2015  as  Obama's  Capitulation  Monday."  Rep.  Ileana  Ros-Lehtinen  (FL-27)  warned,  "The 
Cuban  people's  oppressors  will  not  hesitate  to  use  this  'embassy'  as  a spy  hub,  as  they 
have  done  in  the  past  to  threaten  our  homeland."  Her  colleague,  Rep.  Mario  Diaz  Balart 
(FL-25)  echoed  her  fears  for  U.S.  national  security,  saying,  "A  Cuban  embassy  will 
represent  the  Cuban  military  and  intelligence  services  that  perpetuate  human  rights  abuses 
against  them."  Senator  Bob  Menendez  dismissed  the  events  as  "empty  ribbon-cutting 
ceremonies." 

While  the  U.S.  Interests  Section  in  Havana  opened  for  business  as  the  Embassy  of  the 
United  States  on  Monday,  as  CNN  reported  , the  festivities  and  flag-raising  will  have  to 
wait  for  Secretary  of  State  John  Kerry's  visit  --  the  highest-level  trip  by  a U.S.  official  to 
Cuba  since  the  1959  revolution  ,"  which  he  announced  on  Monday  will  take  place  on 
August  14th. 

Speculation  is  already  turning  to  whether  President  Obama  will  visit  Cuba  before  the  end 
of  his  term  in  office  in  January  2017.  El  Nuevo  Herald  reported  this  week  that  a 
decision  on  a possible  trip  would  be  evaluated  early  next  year  "based  on  the  progress 
achieved  by  Cuban  authorities  on  issues  that  the  U.S.  government  considers  to  be 
important,  such  as  human  rights." 

Senate  Appropriations  Committee  adopts  amendments  to  allow  Cuba  travel  and 
trade 

On  Thursday,  the  Senate  Appropriations  Committee  approved  three  amendments  to  expand 
travel  and  trade  with  Cuba  as  it  considered  legislation  funding  the  U.S.  Treasury 
Department  and  other  agencies,  reports  the  Washington  Post.  These  were  the  first 
successful  appropriations  amendments  this  year  that  ease  restrictions  on  Cuba  policy,  and 
they  passed  with  bipartisan  support. 

Kansas  Senator  Jerry  Moran's  amendment  to  end  the  travel  ban  to  Cuba  was  passed  by  an 
18-12  vote.  "I'm  of  the  view  that  we  have  the  opportunity  to  increase  the  likelihood  that 
the  Cuban  people  have  greater  liberties  and  freedom  with  the  ability  to  connect  with  them," 
said  Sen.  Moran  following  the  vote.  Sen.  Patrick  Leahy  (VT)  pointed  out  that  U.S.  citizens 
are  free  to  travel  to  any  other  country,  even  North  Korea  and  Iran,  with  which  relations 
are  even  more  strained.  "The  only  country  where  Americans  are  told  they  can't  go  and 
spend  their  own  money  is  Cuba,"  Leahy  said.  "It  does  not  make  sense.  We  ought  to  be 
allowed  to  go  there." 

Sen.  Jon  Tester  (MT)  offered  an  amendment  to  end  the  180-day  quarantine  of  maritime 
vessels  coming  from  Cuba  to  the  U.S.  Sen.  John  Boozman  (AR)  also  got  his  proposal 
through  the  Committee  to  "repeal  a law  that  prohibits  banks  and  other  U.S.  businesses 
from  financing  sales  of  U.S.  agricultural  exports  to  Cuba,"  as  Arkansas  Online  described 

10/17/2016 

This  version  of  Total  Mail  Converter  is  not  registered. 

Page  767 

the  measure.  Both  amendments  were  adopted  on  voice  votes. 

Their  amendments  are  now  included  in  what  is  called  The  FY2016  Financial  Services  and 
General  Government  Appropriations  bill,  which  would  next  be  considered  by  the  full 
Senate. 

As  we  have  previously  reported  , funding  bills  written  in  the  U.S.  Flouse  of 
Representatives  include  provisions  that  seek  to  roll  back  and  prevent  further  policy 
changes  that  would  open  relations  with  Cuba. 

Support  in  the  Senate  for  maintaining  and  advancing  more  open  relations  with  Cuba  was 
also  evident  in  the  State  Department  funding  bill  approved  earlier  this  month,  when 
Senator  Lindsey  Graham  (SC)  was  unable  to  find  the  votes  for  his  amendment  to  cut-off 
funding  for  the  U.S.  Embassy  in  Flavana.  Before  becoming  law,  the  Flouse  and  Senate 
appropriations  bills  must  be  reconciled  in  a conference  - including  reaching  agreement  on 
how  to  handle  pro-opening  and  pro-sanctions  amendments  - after  which  identical 
measures  must  clear  the  Flouse  and  Senate  before  being  presented  to  the  President. 

The  White  Flouse  has  already  begun  advising  Congress  that  President  Obama  will  veto 
bills  that  attempt  to  reverse  the  new  policy  of  engagement  with  Cuba. 

Businesses  and  policymakers  seek  to  expand  trade  and  telecommunications  with 
Cuba 

Airbnb,  MasterCard,  and  Netflix  are  among  the  companies  seeking  to  position  themselves 
favorably  in  Cuba  for  the  time  when  U.S.  fmns  can  do  business  freely  on  the  island.  At  the 
same  time,  lawmakers  are  seeking  to  address  embargo  restrictions  through  permanent 
changes  in  law,  reports  U.S.  News  and  World  Reports. 

Congressman  Kevin  Cramer  (ND-At  large)  introduced  bipartisan  legislation  with  Rep. 
Peter  Welch  (VT-At  large)  that  would  enable  U.S.  telecommunications  firms  to  offer 
services  in  Cuba.  The  legislation  is  an  identical  Flouse  version  of  the  Cuba  DATA  Act, 
introduced  in  the  Senate  by  Sen.  Tom  Udall  (NM),  as  we  reported  in  May.  Increasing 
affordable  Internet  access  in  Cuba  is  a priority  for  Cubans,  particularly  the  small  but 
growing  class  of  technology  entrepreneurs  on  the  island. 

A 2014  study  by  Freedom  House  found  that  only  26%  of  Cubans  have  basic  Internet 
access  and  less  than  5%  have  unrestricted  access  to  broadband  connections.  A central 
impediment  is  cost.  Typical  hourly  access  at  a government-run  Internet  cafe  is  more  than 
$4,  roughly  a fifth  of  the  average  Cuban  monthly  salary.  The  state -run  telecommunications 
company  Etecsa  has  recently  opened  35  new  public  internet  hot-spots  and  reduced  the 
price  to  about  $2  per  hour  to  bring  the  Internet  more  within  reach.  This  is  part  of  Cuba's 
long-term  plan  to  bring  broadband  access  to  half  of  the  island's  homes  by  2020. 

Speaking  about  his  bill,  Rep.  Cramer  said,  "Not  only  would  our  telecommunications 
companies  have  the  opportunity  to  upgrade  Cuba's  infrastructure,  but  our  farmers  and 
entrepreneurs  would  be  able  to  conduct  business  in  Cuba  utilizing  2 1 st  century 
communication  methods." 

Banking  agreement  with  Cuba  will  facilitate  U.S.  business  deals 

On  Tuesday,  Stonegate  Bank  of  Pompano  Beach,  Florida  announced  that  it  has  reached  a 
deal  with  Banco  Intemacional  de  Comercio  S.A.  (BICSA)  to  open  the  first  correspondent 
account  with  Cuba.  The  Wall  Street  Journal  reports  that  the  account,  which  will  allow 
direct  payment  and  transactions  between  the  U.S.  and  Cuba  without  going  through  a third 
country,  will  be  up  and  running  within  three  to  four  weeks.  As  we  reported  in  May, 
Stonegate  previously  agreed  to  open  a commercial  bank  account  for  transactions  used  by 
Cuba  for  its  consular  and  diplomatic  operations  in  the  U.S. 

Banking  regulators  in  the  U.S.  closely  scrutinize  transactions  with  foreign  countries  via 

10/17/2016 

This  version  of  Total  Mail  Converter  is  not  registered. 

Page  768 

correspondent  accounts,  particularly  in  countries  considered  to  present  risks  for  money 
laundering  or  criminal  activity.  The  Financial  Action  Task  Force  (FATF),  a multilateral 
organization  that  combats  international  money  laundering,  listed  Cuba  as  a "high  risk" 
country  in  2014,  but  recently  praised  Cuba  for  taking  strong  actions  to  police  its  financial 
system.  As  we  reported  in  October  2014,  FATF  has  ceased  to  monitor  Cuba  for 
compliance  with  anti-money-laundering  and  anti-terrorist  finance  rules,  due  to  its  progress 
in  domestic  enforcement. 

Of  the  decision  to  pursue  direct  ties  with  BICSA,  Stonegate  Bank  president  Dave  Seleski 
told  reporters,  "We  did  an  extensive  risk-management  approach  to  this...  We  feel  very 
comfortable  that  we  did  something  that  is  very  low  risk." 

Peterson  Institute  economist  Gary  Hufbauer  cites  the  development  as  an  important  step  in 
facilitating  business  between  the  U.S.  and  Cuba.  The  move  lays  basic  groundwork  for  the 
future  use  of  U.S.  credit  cards  in  Cuba,  which  are  allowed  under  Treasury  Department 
regulations  announced  in  January.  Atlantic  Council  analyst  Jason  Marczak  agrees  that 
credit  will  be  important  as  travel  and  tourism  to  the  island  increases. 

Cuba  may  drill  for  oil  using  U.S.  equipment 

As  Cuba  continues  to  pursue  offshore  drilling  in  the  Gulf  of  Mexico  to  explore  for 
commercially-viable  deposits  of  petroleum,  the  Obama  Administration  has  put  into  place  a 
new  policy  that  "calls  for  the  U.S.  Department  of  Commerce  to  license  for  export  to  Cuba 
any  items  deemed  necessary  for  protection  of  U.S.  coastal  environments,"  the  Tampa 
Tribune  reports. 

Under  the  embargo,  equipment  containing  more  than  ten  percent  U.S. -made  or  -developed 
technology  cannot  be  used  for  economic  activity  in  Cuba.  Oil  industry  and  environmental 
experts  are  concerned  with  this  restriction,  arguing  that  that  superior  U.S.  equipment 
should  be  used  to  provide  the  best  protection  and  mitigation  of  possible  oil  spills  and 
resultant  ecological  disasters,  as  CDA  found  in  our  report  on  Cuba's  plans  to  drill  in  the 
Gulf  of  Mexico. 

Lee  Hunt,  a Houston-based  oil  expert  who  helped  organize  a multilateral  coordination  on 
future  spills  following  the  20 1 0 Deepwater  Horizon  disaster,  is  now  spearheading  a 
symposium  in  Havana  in  October  20 1 5 to  further  deepen  the  cooperation  between  the 
U.S.,  Cuba,  Mexico,  Jamaica,  and  the  Bahamas.  Hunt  maintains  that  "It  is  in  our  benefit  to 
want  every  drilling  operation  in  Cuba  to  have  the  same  standard  as  is  mandatory  in  the 
U.S.  for  the  prevention  of  pollution." 

Licensing  under  the  new  Commerce  Department  policy  would  enable  that.  As  Dan  Whittle, 
Cuba  program  director  at  Environmental  Defense  Fund,  says  "The  new  rules  give 
favorable  review  to  certain  kinds  of  exports  including  those  in  the  environmental  sector 
that  benefit  the  U.S." 

Jorge  Pinon,  director  of  the  Latin  America  and  Caribbean  Energy  Program  at  the 
University  of  Texas,  believes  the  regulation  can  be  interpreted  even  more  broadly.  "An 
argument  can  made  that  you  need  every  piece  of  its  equipment  to  be  top  notch  because  if 
any  one  fails  during  drilling,  there  can  be  an  accident,"  Pinon  said.  "So  make  the  whole  rig 
exempt  from  the  10  percent  rule." 

The  rule  itself  as  it  applies  to  oil  rig  equipment  may  now  be  changing.  This  week  the 
Commerce  Department  implemented  new  regulations  following  the  removal  of  Cuba 
from  the  State  Sponsors  of  Terrorism,  permitting  the  re-export  to  Cuba  of  foreign-made 
products  with  up  to  25%  U.S. -origin  content. 

Cuba's  government  plans  to  drill  two  deep  water  wells  by  the  end  of  20 1 6 and  has 
received  interest  from  Angola's  Sonangol  and  Venezuela's  PDVS.  However,  the 
advanced  Norwegian-built  offshore  rig  Scarabeo  9,  which  was  built  specially  in  China  to 
ensure  U.S.  content  was  below  the  10%  legal  limit,  and  was  previously  used  to  explore 

10/17/2016 

This  version  of  Total  Mail  Converter  is  not  registered. 

Page  769 

offshore  in  Cuban  waters  in  2012,  may  not  be  available  in  the  timeframe  desired  by  Cuban 
authorities. 

CUBA'S  FOREIGN  RELATIONS 

Latin  America  says  yes  to  greater  U.S.-Cuba  diplomatic  ties 

A new  survey  by  the  Pew  Research  Center  found  that  majorities  in  Latin  America  strongly 
support  closer  U.S.-Cuba  relations,  reports  NBC  News.  A median  of  77%  of  respondents 
across  five  Latin  American  countries  approve  of  the  U.S.  re-establishing  diplomatic 
relations  with  Cuba.  The  strongest  support  was  found  in  Chile  (79%),  Argentina  (78%), 
and  Venezuela  (77%),  followed  by  Brazil  (67%)  and  Mexico  (54%). 

When  asked  their  opinions  about  the  U.S.  trade  embargo  against  Cuba,  Latin  Americans 
overwhelmingly  supported  lifting  the  embargo:  Argentina  (79%),  Chile  (77%),  Venezuela 
(76%),  Brazil  (71%),  and  Mexico  (55%). 

The  poll  found  that  respondents  with  higher  incomes  tended  to  more  strongly  support 
ending  the  embargo  than  lower-income  respondents.  In  Argentina,  the  income  divide  was 
most  evident,  with  82%  of  high  earners  supporting  and  66%  of  lower  earners  in  support. 
Overall  opinions  of  Cuba  were  split  across  the  six  countries  surveyed:  a median  40%  of 
respondents  view  Cuba  favorably  while  44%  view  Cuba  unfavorably.  Chileans  showed  the 
strongest  favorable  feelings  about  Cuba  at  49%,  while  majorities  of  Brazilians  and 
Mexicans  view  Cuba  negatively.  Leaders  of  Latin  American  countries  have  widely 
praised  the  thaw  in  U.S.-Cuba  relations. 

German  minister  is  pleased  by  results  of  his  visit  to  Cuba 

German  Foreign  Minister  Frank-Walter  Steinmeier  expressed  optimism  following  his 
recent  trip  to  Cuba,  reports  Progreso  Weekly.  Minister  Steinmeier  spent  two  days  in 
Flavana  meeting  with  senior  government  officials  and  visiting  agricultural  sites. 

President  Castro  and  Minister  Steinmeier  met  for  almost  two  hours  to  discuss  how  Cuba 
can  open  up  to  increased  foreign  investment,  an  important  cornerstone  of  Cuba's 
economic  plans.  Steinmeier  sees  potential  for  German  companies  to  invest  in  several 
sectors  in  Cuba,  including  medical  technology,  logistics,  renewable  energy,  and  especially 
agriculture.  Germany  is  already  involved  in  Cuban  agriculture  through  donations  that  help 
fund  the  urban  Havana  farm  Vivero  Alamar  . 

Steinmeier  also  addressed  human  rights  concerns  in  meetings  with  Cuban  officials. 
Following  the  trip  he  said,  "We  will  continue  to  hold  different  views  on  our  attitudes  to 
democracy  and  human  rights  concerns.  But  right  now  we  want  to  try  to  get  past  the  phase 
of  mutism...  I believe  that  this  is  the  right  time  to  readjust  our  relations." 

A key  result  of  Steinmeier's  trip  was  the  signing  of  framework  accords  to  further 
formalize  bilateral  relations,  which  included  commitments  to  respect  human  rights.  This  is 
in  keeping  with  the  evolution  of  the  European  Union  Common  Position  on  Cuba.  The  EU 
is  in  talks  with  Cuba  to  improve  bilateral  relations,  and  hopes  to  have  more  formalized 
accords  by  the  end  of  the  year. 

IN  CUBA

Resources  Institute  (Institute)  Nacional  de  Recursos  Hidraulicos,  or  INRH),  May  and  June

saw  less  than  1 1 inches  of  rain,  less  than  75%  of  the  normal  amount  for  this  time  period. 
The  drought  is  being  felt  most  acutely  on  the  western  side  of  the  island,  which  has 
received  71%  of  its  normal  rainfall  so  far  in  2015. 

Cuba's  water  reservoirs  are  currently  at  37%  of  their  capacity  on  average.  More  than  160 
reservoirs  are  at  less  than  50%  and  1 1 1 are  down  below  25%  capacity.  The  current 
drought  began  in  late  2014,  affecting  more  than  half  the  country  and  putting  pressure  on 
farms,  livestock,  and  drinking  water  supplies. 

Cuba  is  no  stranger  to  natural  disasters  associated  with  hydro-meteorological  events,  such 
as  droughts  and  hurricanes.  The  island  endured  a severe  drought  in  2004-2005,  which 
affected  the  entire  country  and  cost  some  $3  billion  in  economic  losses.  The  current 
drought  and  lack  of  reserves  led  President  Castro  to  call  for  water  rationing  last  week 
during  the  plenary  session  of  the  National  Assembly. 

CORRECTING  THE  RECORD 

Thanks  to  one  observant  reader,  we  made  a weekend  correction  to  last  week's  opening 
essay.  In  the  version  we  circulated  by  email,  we  were  mistaken  in  writing  that  the  U.S. 
flag  would  be  raised  at  the  new  U.S.  embassy  in  Havana  on  July  20.  In  fact,  as  we  report 
above,  that  will  not  take  place  until  August  14th  when  Secretary  Kerry  will  be  in 
attendance.  The  corrected  version  appears  here  , and  we  apologize  for  an  instance  when 
we  permitted  the  rhetoric  to  get  ahead  of  the  facts. 

Recommended  Reading 

Hope  Takes  Over  Havana  , James  Williams  and  Ricardo  Herrero,  Miami  Herald 

James  Williams,  President  of  Engage  Cuba  Coalition,  and  Ricardo  Herrero,  Executive 
Director  of  CubaNow,  talk  about  their  optimism  for  the  future  of  U.S. -Cuba  relations 
following  their  recent  trip  to  the  island. 

Regime  change  or  not?  , Manuel  Gomez,  Progreso  Weekly 

Manuel  Gomez  discusses  U.S.  attitudes  towards  opening  relations  with  Cuba,  and 
examines  possible  underlying  regime  change  motivations  he  observes  in  the  rhetoric  of 
prominent  U.S.  policymakers  who  support  engagement  with  Cuba.  Mr.  Gomez  serves  as  a 
board  member  of  the  Center  for  Democracy  in  the  Americas,  which  publishes  the  Cuba 
Central  News  Blast. 

Cuba  and  America:  The  End  of  an  Estrangement  , Jon  Lee  Anderson,  The  New 
Yorker 

Jon  Lee  Anderson  argues  that  both  the  U.S.  and  Cuba  have  benefitted  on  the  whole  from 
restoring  relations. 

What's  Next  for  Cuba  and  the  U.S.?  , Editorial  Board,  The  New  York  Times 

The  New  York  Times  Editorial  Board  characterizes  the  internal  debates  that  must  take 
place  in  Cuba  as  the  governments  of  Cuba  and  the  U.S.  proceed  in  deepening  ties. 

Why  African  Americans  Should  Be  1st  in  Line  to  Cuba  , DeWayne  Wickham,  The 
Root 

DeWayne  Wickham  describes  historical  ties  between  African  Americans  and  Afro-Cubans 
and  urges  African  Americans  to  visit  Cuba. 

How  to  Build  a Relationship  With  Havana  , James  Stavridis,  Foreign  Policy

Former  NATO  Supreme  Allied  Commander  James  Stavridis  offers  ideas  to  build  on 
existing  areas  of  U.S.-Cuba  cooperation  to  deepen  ties  constructively,  with  an  eye  to 
geopolitics. 

Not  Your  Grandma's  Cuba:  A New  Day  in  the  Caribbean  , Otaviano  Canuto, 
WorldPost 

IMF  Executive  Director  Otaviano  Canuto  describes  the  complicated  economic  and  political 
transitions  in  Cuba  and  urges  constructive  engagement  by  the  U.S.  and  other  countries. 

Passage  to  Cuba:  An  Up-Close  Look  at  the  World's  Most  Colorful  Culture  , 
Cynthia  Carris  Alonso,  Skyhorse  Publishing 

Veteran  photojoumalist  Cynthia  Carris  Alonso  has  captured  Cuban  life  in  many  visits  to  the 
island  over  the  past  20  years.  "Passage  to  Cuba"  is  her  first  book  and  was  released  this 
summer  to  critical  acclaim. 

21  US  MDs  Graduate  from  Cuba's  Latin  American  Medical  School  , MEDICC 

Havana's  Latin  American  Medical  School  (ELAM),  the  world's  largest  socially-accountable 
medical  school,  graduated  21  new  MDs  from  the  U.S.  on  Tuesday.  This  brings  the  total  to 
136  U.S.  doctors  trained  in  Cuba  since  ELAM's  founding  in  1999. 

A Timeline  of  U.S.-Cuba  Rapprochement  , Elizabeth  Gonzalez,  Americas  Society/ 
Council  of  the  Americas 

Elizabeth  Gonzalez  presents  an  infographic  timeline  of  how  the  U.S.  and  Cuba  came  to 
restore  diplomatic  relations,  beginning  with  the  first  meeting  between  White  House  officials 
and  Cuban  officials  in  Ottawa  in  June  2013. 

Recommended  Viewing 

Interview  with  Jose  Pertierra  and  Peter  Kornbluh  at  Opening  of  Cuban  Embassy 
in  Washington.  Amy  Goodman,  Democracy  Now! 

Amy  Goodman  interviews  Jose  Pertierra,  the  prominent  immigration  attorney  and  Cuba 
expert,  and  Peter  Kornbluh  , director  of  the  Cuba  Documentation  Project  at  the  National 
Security  Archive  and  co-author  of  "Back  Channel  to  Cuba,"  the  morning  of  July  20l11,  just 
an  hour  before  the  Cuban  flag  was  raised  above  the  Embassy. 

Cuba's  Foreign  Minister  Talks  With  David  Muir  About  Historic  "New  Chapter"  in

Cuban  Foreign  Minister  Bruno  Rodriguez  talks  with  ABC's  David  Muir  from  the  newly  re- 
designated Cuban  Embassy  in  Washington,  DC. 

Secretary  of  State  John  Kerry  and  Cuban  Foreign  Minister  Bruno  Rodriguez

Cuban  Embassy  Flag  Raising  Ceremony  , C-Span 

U.S.-Cuba  relations  were  officially  restored  with  the  re-opening  of  the  Cuban  Embassy  in

outside  the  Cuban  Embassy.

"As  an  Indian-American  who  has  lived  in  this  country  since  the  age  of  four,  serving  in  the  Obama-Biden  campaign  (and  now  the 
Obama-Biden  transition  team)  is  a uniquely  great  honor  for  me.  I am  proud  of  my  service  as  an  official  of  the  United  States 
government  through  two  Administrations,  working  in  Bosnia,  Kosovo,  Southeast  Asia,  Africa  and  Eastern  Europe—  but  I believe 
that  the  election  of  Barack  Obama  represents  a sea-change  in  relations  between  America  and  the  global  community.  I'm  proud  of 
my  involvement  in  the  campaign  and  transition—  not  just  for  myself,  but  also  for  what  my  selection  says  about  the  Indian- 
American  community.  This  campaign  has  truly  sought  out  the  voices  and  talents  of  South  Asian  Americans  in  a way  never  before 
seen—  and  I have  every  expectation  that  this  attitude  will  be  carried  over  to  the  new  Administration. 

"A  presidential  transition  is  always  a time  of  wild  rumors  and  unfounded  gossip,  so  I'd  like  to  set  to  rest  a few  baseless 
reports  that  have  been  circulating  on  the  Internet: 

—First,  I've  never  been  affiliated—  in  any  way,  shape  or  form—  with  any  Indian  political  party  or  similar  group.  To  clear  up 
one  false  rumor:  I've  never  been  affiliated  with  the  Vishwa  Flindu  Parishad  (VFiP)  the  Rashtriya  Swayamsevak  Sangh  (RSS),  or  any 
such  organization.  I've  never  been  involved  in  Indian  politics,  and  never  intend  to  do  so. 

—Second,  my  personal  politics  have  nothing  in  common  with  the  views  espoused  by  such  groups.  I've  always  condemned 
any  politics  of  division,  of  ethnic  or  religious  hatred,  of  violence  and  intimidation  as  a political  tool.  That's  why  I've  devoted  so 
much  of  the  past  two  years  to  the  candidacy  of  a figure  who  truly  does  represent  my  personal  political  views:  Barack  Obama. 

—Third,  some  Internet  rumors  have  attempted  to  link  me  to  Flindu  Nationalist  groups  through  a variety  of  tenuous 
connections:  Relief  work  I'm  proud  to  have  helped  coordinate  following  the  Gujarati  earthquake  of  2001,  or  cultural  and 
religious  affiliations  of  some  of  my  family  members,  or  apolitical  humanitarian  work  I've  been  privileged  to  do  as  a founder  of 
the  NGO  Indicorps  and  as  the  Director  of  Global  Development  for  Google.org.  I have  no  ties  to  any  such  groups,  and  never  have. 
We  saw  too  much  guilt  by  association  during  the  presidential  campaign-  and  we  saw  such  tactics  decisively  repudiated  by  the 
American  people. 

"I  am  delighted  with  what  the  victory  on  November  4 says  about  my  country,  and  about  our  place  in  the  world.  For  too  long, 
Americans  of  South  Asian  descent  have  been  made  to  feel  as  if  we  can't  be  proudly  desi  yet  fully  American.  For  too  long,  we've 
had  to  ask  ourselves  whether  we  can  overcome  this  unfair  and  baseless  exclusion.  Last  Tuesday—  to  my  enormous  pride  and 
satisfaction—  America  gave  its  reply:  Yes,  We  Can!."

constitutionalvalues.org 

FOR  IMMEDIATE  RELEASE 
Wednesday,  May  27,  2009 

New  TV  Spot:  “Justice”  Introduces  Americans  to  Judge 

Sonia  Sotomayor 

Watch  the  Spot  on  ConstitutionalValues.org 

Washington,  DC  - The  Coalition  for  Constitutional  Values,  a national  coalition  of  the  nation’s  leading  nonprofit  and 
advocacy  organizations,  announced  today  that  it  will  begin  airing  “Justice,”  a new  30-second  television  spot  that  will  run 
on  national  network  news  and  cable  news  starting  today. 

“This  spot  introduces  the  American  people  to  Judge  Sonia  Sotomayor.  Every  aspect  of  American  life  is  affected  by  our 
justice  system,”  said  Wade  Henderson,  co-chair  of  the  Coalition  for  Constitutional  Values  and  president  of  the  Leadership 
Conference  on  Civil  Rights.  “It’s  important  that  they  understand  her  fair-minded  approach  to  the  law,  which  is  grounded  both 
in  her  eminent  legal  qualifications  and  her  life  experiences.” 

The  Coalition  for  Constitutional  Values,  whose  members  represent  millions  of  Americans,  believes  it  is  important  that  the 
American  people  know  about  the  qualities  of  their  Supreme  Court  justices. 

"In  selecting  Judge  Sotomayor,  the  president  has  nominated  a candidate  of  sterling  credentials  who  will  uphold  the 
Constitution  and  the  law,”  said  Nan  Aron,  co-chair  of  the  Coalition  for  Constitutional  Values  and  president  of  Alliance  for 
Justice.  “We  commend  President  Obama  for  choosing  a brilliant  and  fair-minded  jurist  to  serve  on  our  nation’s  highest 
court.  Judge  Sotomayor  is  precisely  the  kind  of  nominee  we  need  - one  who,  as  President  Obama  described,  ‘has  the 
intellectual  firepower  but  also  a little  bit  of  a common  touch  and  has  a practical  sense  of  how  the  world  works.’” 

“President  Obama  used  this  opportunity  to  do  exactly  what  he  promised  in  last  year’s  election — to  select  a person  who 
has  demonstrated  an  abiding  commitment  to  core  constitutional  values  of  justice,  opportunity,  and  equality  under  the  law. 
He  has  named  someone  who  understands  the  impact  that  the  law  has  on  the  everyday  lives  of  ordinary  Americans,”  said 
Michael  B.  Keegan,  co-chair  of  the  Coalition  for  Constitutional  Values  and  president  of  People  For  the  American  Way. 

The  new  spot  is  part  of  a broader  public  education  campaign  launched  by  the  Coalition  for  Constitutional  Values,  co- 
chaired by  the  Leadership  Conference  on  Civil  Rights,  Alliance  for  Justice  and  People  For  the  American  Way.  The  Coalition 
hopes  the  spot  will  introduce  the  American  public  to  Judge  Sotomayor,  who  has  experience  in  nearly  every  aspect  of  the 
law,  having  served  as  a big-city  prosecutor  and  a corporate  litigator,  a federal  trial  judge,  and  an  appellate  judge. 

Watch  the  spot  online  at  ConstitutionalValues.org.  The  full  script  is  below. 

“ Justice”

PROGRESS 

OHIO 

November  23,  2015 
For  Immediate  Release 

New  Video  Spotlights  Ohio’s  Assault  on  Reproductive  Rights 

COLUMBUS--The  anti-choice  movement’s  pattern  of  quietly  slipping  abortion  restrictions  into  state  budget 
bills  has  resulted  in  two  dangerous  trends: 

Ohio  is  now  home  to  some  of  America’s  harshest  anti-abortion  laws;  and  many  women  are  unaware  that  their 
reproductive  rights  have  been  systematically  curtailed. 

A new  video  by  Majority  Ohio  aims  to  tell  Ohio  voters  what’s  really  happening. 

"A  series  of  woman-on-the-street  interviews  showed  a strong  majority  think  that  it’s  about  as  easy  to  get  an 
abortion  today  as  it  was  after  Roe  vs  Wade  made  abortion  legal  in  1973,"  said  Majority  Ohio  CEO  Cliff  Schecter. 
"In  reality,  it’s  much  harder.  In  the  past  5 years  alone,  half  of  Ohio’s  abortion  clinics  have  been  forced  to  close 
and  the  state  has  added  16  new  restrictions." 

The  Ohio  interviews  mirror  a series  of  nationwide  focus  groups  conducted  by  the  National  Institute  for 
Reproductive  Health  showing  that  most  women  are  unaware  of  the  concerted  efforts  to  restrict  access  to 
abortion  and  shutter  clinics,  said  ProgressOhio  Executive  Director  Sandy  Theis,  who  observed  some  of  the 
focus  groups. 

"When  women  are  presented  with  the  truth  about  the  laws  that  restrict  abortion  access,  they  are  shocked," 
Theis  said.  "When  they  learned  this  has  been  happening  behind  their  backs,  they  grow  angry  and  want  to 
reverse  this  trend  around." 

New  restrictions  include  requiring  medically  unnecessary  ultrasounds,  cuts  in  funding  for  Planned  Parenthood, 
a ban  on  talking  to  rape  survivors  about  abortion  under  some  circumstances,  a late-term  abortion  ban, 
requiring  clinics  to  have  unnecessary  agreements  with  hospitals  and  preventing  public  hospitals  from  joining 
those  agreements,  and  strengthening  the  state  health  director's  authority  to  refuse  exceptions  to  the 
agreements. 

Ohio  is  not  alone.  Nationwide,  there  have  been  more  than  1,000  new  restrictions  since  Roe  vs.  Wade. 

The  new  video  comes  on  the  heels  of  an  Associated  Press  report  documenting  that  aides  to  Gov.  John 
Kasich  methodically  worked  behind  the  scenes  to  help  shape  some  restrictions,  while  the  governor  publicly 
portrayed  his  office  as  neutral  when  the  provisions  began  to  generate  opposition  from  major  newspapers  and 
abortion  rights  groups. 

"Gov.  Kasich  intentionally  concealed  his  role  in  the  assault  on  women’s  reproductive  rights  because  he  did  not 

10/17/2016 

This  version  of  Total  Mail  Converter  is  not  registered. 

Page  790 

want  to  risk  alienating  the  majority  of  Ohio  voters,"  Theis  said. 

Majority  Ohio  is  a non-partisan,  non-profit  created  to  elevate  women’s  economic  and  health  care  issues 
during  the  presidential  campaign.  ProgressOhio  is  among  its  coalition  partners.

From:  "Ruth  Greenspan  Bell"  <Ruth.Bell@wilsoncenter.ora> 
To:  "Ruth  Greenspan  Bell"  <ruthareenspanbell@amail.com> 
Date:  1 1/12/2014  9:40:38  AM 

Subject:  greenhouse  gas  reductions  and  our  built  environment 

Can  small  changes  in  how  design  options  are  presented  to  engineers  and  architects  achieve  greater  energy  savings  in  the 
infrastructure  they  produce?  My  colleagues  Elke  Weber  and  Tripp  Shealy  discuss  cutting  edge  research  that  supports  this 
proposition  and  offers  alternative  pathways  toward  greenhouse  gas  reductions:  http://www.dailvclimate.org/tdc-newsroom/ 
2014/11/opinion-better-solutions 

Once  the  buildings  we  live  in  or  the  highways  where  we  drive  are  built,  the  options  for  reducing  energy  consumption  are 
considerably  narrowed,  even  if  we  want  to  do  better.  Construction  locks  in  decisions  about  materials,  heating,  cooling,  lighting, 
and  modes  of  transportation. 

We  know  that  small  changes  in  how  options  are  presented  to  decisionmakers,  or  pre-selecting  an  option  as  a default,  can  trigger 
big  change  because  we  have  seen  this  happen  to  improve  retirement  savings  or  organ  donor  rates.  Weber  and  Shealy  argue  the 
same  applies  to  energy  efficiency  in  our  structures. 

Ruth  Greenspan  Bell 

Public  Policy  Scholar,  Woodrow  Wilson  International  Center  for  Scholars

Friend, 

If  you’re  like  me,  you  probably  don’t  need  anything  fancier  than

more  than  $140,000  to  join. 

The  Washington  Post  put  it  best:  Rauner  "spends  more  on 
wine  than  average  Illinois  households  spend  on  everything." 

Want  to  show  Rauner  just  how  out  of  touch  that  is?  How  about 
donating  the  price  of  a cheap  bottle  of  wine  to  send  him  a message. 

Chip  in  two  bucks  or  more  to  help  prevent  this  clueless 
billionaire  from  becoming  governor. 

Spending  $100,000  on  wine  is  crazy  to  me. 

But  then  again,  so  is  lowering  the  minimum  wage  --  something  Bruce 
Rauner  actually  proposed,  as  if  a full-time  worker  isn’t  worth  even 
$16,500  a year. 

That’s  not  just  out  of  touch  --  that’s  dangerous.  Because  if  we  don't 
stop  him,  this  could  be  the  person  making  decisions  for  all  of  Illinois. 

Chip  in  $2  or  more  to  make  sure  that  never  happens: 

https://www.quinnforillinois.com/wine-club 

Cheers, 

Carrie

John  — 

I hope  you’re  taking  the  time  to  decompress  a little  before  the  campaign  kicks  in. 

I hope  you  don’t  mind  me  reaching  out,  but  I wanted  to  connect  you  with  a very  good  (and  talented)  friend  of 
mine,  Matt  Littman,  who  is  very  interested  in  helping  on  the  campaign  any  way  he  can,  particularly  in  California. 

I believe  Matt  could  help  the  campaign  in  several  ways: 

First,  he  was  the  head  of  government  relations  at  Broadcom  and  spent  the  last  several  years  working  with  the 
tech  companies  in  California  to  lead  the  effort  on  patent  trolls.  The  coalition  featured  12  companies,  including 
Apple  and  Google,  as  well  as  the  car  companies.  He  has  organized  numerous  dinners  both  in  DC  and  CA  with 
his  friends  at  the  tech  companies,  and  others  involved  in  technology  policy,  with  members  of  Congress.  Thus,  he 
has  great  familiarity  and  relationships  with  many  of  the  players  in  Silicon  Valley  and  elsewhere  that  could  be 
useful  to  the  campaign. 

Second,  he  has  been  a speechwriter  and  screen  writer.  For  speechwriting,  he  has  worked  with  several  political 
figures,  CEOs,  famous  actors  and  sports  figures.  He  worked  with  then  Senator  Biden  in  2007,  and  has  worked 
closely  with  Lehane  and  Fabiani. 

Most  importantly,  Matt  has  a tremendous  amount  of  humor,  common  sense  and  commitment. 

I would  love  to  connect  the  two  of  you  for  a conversation  (over  coffee  or  otherwise)  to  see  how  Matt  could  help 
the  campaign,  whether  it  is  with  relationships  in  California,  writing  and  communicating,  or  anything  else. 

I have  attached  Matt’s  resume  below. 

BTW  — I assume  you  already  know,  but  I’m  also  happy  to  help  any  way  I can. 

Thanks  very  much, 

All  the  best,

Dear  John  - It  was  great  to  attend  the  National  Clean  Energy  Summit  8.0  for  the  fourth  time,  and  note 
all  the  progress  that  has  been  and  is  continuing  to  be  made  particularly  in  the  Western  States  with 
regards  to  major  Renewable  Energy  Projects  that  have  are  now  completed  and  in  the  near  future  are 
coming  online.  I was  also  pleased  to  hear  that  a major  topic  is  now  the  National  Clean  Energy  Plan 
being  articulated  including  moving  towards  modernizing  the  National  Grid  to  a Smart  Grid. 

I very  much  appreciate  the  short  conversation  that  we  had  at  the  very  end  of  the  day 
regarding  GrowGreen  Power's  Mission  along  with  very  briefly  showing  you  the  thesis  of  The  United 
States  - Sustainable  Cities  & Infrastructure  Planning  Initiative  for  a United  and  Sustainable  Clean 
Energy  America  by  the  Year  2050.  I appreciate  that  you  took  the  time  for  our  conversation  at  the  end 
of  a long,  and  really  great  day  with  President  Obama  arriving  at  the  conclusion  of  the  event.  Your 
contribution  along  with  Senator  Reid's  during  the  eight  years  of  the  Clean  Energy  Summit  is  to  be  highly 
commended.  Making  progress  on  Renewable  Energy  during  an  increasingly  divided  time  in  our  Nation's 
History  has  not  been  easy  but  we  are  getting  there. 

I believe  within  this  message  and  the  attachments  I am  sending  are  important  key  strategy  points,  both 
technical  and  political,  that  I am  offering  to  contribute  to  understand  how  the  United  States  can  lead 
again  with  a clear  comprehensive  National  Vision  understood  by  all.  This  will  come  with  a compelling 
unifying  reason  that  will  bring  Americans  back  together  with  an  Aligned  Vision  Plan.  The  major  points 
of  this  Vision  Plan  are  in  the  attachments  that  are  would  greatly  accelerate  the  forward  progress  with 
renewed  American  Leadership  in  the  World  Community  on  the  path  to  a Sustainable  21st  Century  by  the 
Year  2050. 

As  I mentioned  to  you,  I originally  talked  with  you  briefly  at  the  2010  National  Clean  Energy  Summit  4.0. 
Two  years  earlier,  based  on  almost  20  years  of  previous  visionary  initiatives  that  I was  involved  in  and 
lead  in  Hawaii  from  1986-96,  that  concerned  Community  Based  Planning  Initiatives,  concepts  for 
Sustainable  Cities,  Sustainable  Eco  Villages  and  Communities,  - I brought  my  partners  together  in 
August  2008  and  formed  GrowGreen  Power  Inc.  Our  purpose  and  mission  was  to  begin  our  endeavor  to 
put  into  a development  plan  GrowGreen  Power  Centers  that  could  be  replicated  in  Major  Cities

Worldwide  and  in  virtually  all  climate  conditions  because  of  our  climate  control  capabilities  utilizing 
waste  thermal  energy  from  the  power  production. 

We  planned  to  design  and  develop  large  commercial  scale  Hydroponic  Greenhouses  combined  with 
Biomass  and/  or  Solar  Thermal  Power  plants  to  address  both  sustainable  food  production  and  a portion 
of  local  Renewable  Energy  production  in  a combined  food  / energy  platform.  We  began  in  August  2008 
right  when  the  National  and  World  Economy  began  its  free  fall  and  shortly  after  that  right  as  President 
Obama  won  the  election.  Two  years  later  in  2010,  we  secured  our  initial  $2.5M  Angel  Funding  to 
proceed  to  advance  GrowGreen  Power  Inc.'s  mission  through  Schematic  Design  Technical  Analysis  of 
Biomass  Plant  / Hydroponic  Greenhouse  - site  selection  50  Miles  from  Charlotte,  NC.  We  are  now 
nearing  completion  of  Phase  1 - securing  the  Financing  for  the  50MW  Biomass  Plant.  The  initiation  of 
the  GrowGreen  Power  endeavor  and  timing  in  2008  with  all  that  was  happening  on  economic  front,  the 
state  of  our  country  with  the  two  wars  the  United  States  was  engaged  in,  and  the  election  of  President 
Obama  are  significant,  and  reaching  out  to  you  now  is  significant  at  this  time  in  2015. 

I would  greatly  appreciate  it  if  you  will  take  the  time  to  review  these  attachments  and  then  connect  with 
me  so  I can  go  over  the  key  central  points.  I believe  you  will  find  within  the  Mission  of  GrowGreen  Power 
and  The  National  Clean  Energy  Vision  Plan  thesis  - key  pieces  of  the  puzzle  for  how  we  will  achieve  the 
massive  undertaking  of  getting  to  a Sustainable  World  Community  by  2050.  These  points  are  important 
to  our  Nation  as  a whole  and  also  to  the  Democratic  Party  winning  this  election  on  all  fronts.  Presidency, 
Senate  and  House  Majority.  This  can  be  done  even  with  the  calculated  strategy  of  division,  of  fear  and 
denial  that  has  continued  to  be  advanced  to  divide  the  country  by  those  unwilling  at  present  to  embrace 
the  future,  and  the  central  truth  that  every  Century  will  bring  dramatic  change  and  challenges  to  be  met. 

GrowGreen  Power  Centers  - Economic  Green  Zones  around  Cities  in  the  United  States  and 
Worldwide: 

If  at  all  possible,  I would  like  to  connect  directly  regarding  the  GrowGreen  Power  Mission  to  develop, 
design,  construct  and  operate  GrowGreenPower  Centers  (Fully  Climate  Controlled  (100 
acre)  Hydroponic  Greenhouses  combined  with  50  MW  Biomass  and/or  Solar  Thermal  Power 
Plants)  in  major  cities  across  the  United  States  and  around  the  World.  GrowGreen  Power  Centers  are  an 
important  key  anchor  component  for  creating  Green  Economic  Zones  around  Cities  and  Communities 
Worldwide.  In  reality,  this  development  strategy  must  move  very  rapidly  to  be  effective  in  time  and  this 
will  need  support  at  a National  Level  to  actually  move  at  the  speed  it  should  with  Climate  Change  and 
Population  Growth  increasing  the  stress  of  Global  food  security,  water  resources  and  energy  resources 
with  each  passing  day. 

It  is  my  view  GGP-Centers  and  the  larger  National  Sustainable  Cities  & Infrastructure  Vision 
Plan  below  are  critical  to  designing  and  developing  Sustainable  Cities  & Infrastructure.  Along  with  clean 
renewable  Energy  Power  enough  for  virtually  all  our  Nation's  Energy  requirements  (mapped  out  across 
the  Continental  United  States  by  the  NREL  over  212,000  GW,  there  is  the  need  for  the  upgraded  Smart 
Grid  that  was  discussed  at  the  Energy  Summit  including  constructing  a cross  continental  - High  Voltage 
Direct  Current  Grid  connecting  the  Eastern  and  Western  Grid,  and  the  building  of  Carbon  Neutral 
SmartTech  Cities  in  the  United  States  and  Worldwide. 

A global  comprehensive  approach  to  Collaborative  Sustainable  Design  Worldwide  has  been  my  passion 
and  mission  throughout  much  of  my  career  as  an  architect.  My  career  path  is  somewhat  unique  as  will 
be  clear  if  you  review  my  resume  at  the  end  of  the  Letter  to  President  Obama.  (See  my  full,  CV  and 
Illustrated  Resume  that  contains  my  early  work  and  Visionary  Initiatives  in  Hawaii  and  Design

The  development  of  GrowGreen  Power  Centers  along  with  Economic  Green  Zones  around  American 
Cities  and  Cites  Worldwide  are  a paradigm  shifting  key  that  will  restore  balance  to  the  American  work

The  United  States  - Sustainable  Cities  & Infrastructure  Planning  Initiative  for  a United  and 
Sustainable  Clean  Energy  America  by  the  Year  2050: 

In  addition  to  GrowGreen  Power,  I want  to  share  with  you  for  consideration  the  comprehensive 
proposition  of  The  United  States  - Sustainable  Cities  & Infrastructure  Planning  Initiative  for  a United  and 
Sustainable  Clean  Energy  America  by  the  Year  2050  in  the  attachments. 

This  thesis  was  delivered  and  received  by  President  Obama  in  2012  during  the  last  election.  As  I 
mentioned  in  our  short  conversation  at  the  Clean  Energy  Summit,  John  Bellamy  was  a contact  that  I had 
made  going  back  to  2009  who  was  interested  in  GrowGreen  Power.  John  delivered  two  shorter 
communications  to  the  President  in  2010  with  some  of  the  earlier  visionary  points.  Then  is  2012,  John 
delivered  this  presentation  with  the  full  size  panels,  when  it  was  finished,  along  with  the  attached 
Summary  Letter  to  President  Obama  just  before  the  second  debate  with  Mitt  Romney  in  the  2012 
Election.  According  to  John,  the  President  and  David  Axelrod  had  a short  time  to  review  the  presentation 
at  Camp  David  - and  it  was  well  received.  I was  told  as  far  as  a next  meeting  that  the  President's  re- 
election  was  a priority  before  a full  presentation  could  be  made.  Right  after  the  election,  many  issues 
on  the  National  and  International  Level  displaced  the  time  to  make  a presentation.  So  far,  I have 
not  received  the  opportunity  to  make  a full  presentation  or  been  able  to  connect  with  John  Bellamy  for  a 
number  of  years  now. 

This  National  Vision  is  a comprehensive  plan  that  has  important  history  and  political  points  to  make 
about  how  to  align  and  bring  to  together  our  Nation,  beyond  our  currently  divided  political  impasse. 
Again,  we  can  lead  as  a Nation  for  a Sustainable  World  Community  on  the  World  Front  with  a great 
common  cause  that  will  only  come  when  high  consensus  occurs  around  common  goals  and  a clear, 
comprehensive  National  Vision  Plan  that  can  be  articulated  which  rises  well  above  the  dividing  noise. 
Bringing  Democrats  and  Republicans  together  is  crucial  and  is  possible  in  my  opinion. 

The  Alignment  Moment  in  American  History  that  can  Unify  our  Nation  - Victory  in  World  War  II 
and  what  Democrats  and  Republicans  did  : 

There  was  a very  clear  moment  in  time  of  our  history  that  is  in  my  view  a key  to  how  the  Democratic 
Party  can  lead  our  Nation  as  a whole-back  to  the  point  of  our  greatest  National  Alignment  which  was 
the  in  years  right  after  Pearl  Harbor.  This  is  when  America  entered  the  War  and  United  in  beyond  all  our 
differences  in  a Common  Cause  to  achieve  Victory  over  Nazi  Germany  and  Victory  over  Japan.  In  the 
moment  that  we  achieved  Victory  in  World  War  II  in  the  Pacific-the  point  that  ended  the  most  violent 
and  destructive  War  in  human  history  with  the  most  violent  and  destructive  weapons,  we  as  a Nation 
came  together  with  our  Allies  to  defeat  the  Fear  / Power  / and  Controlling  Forces  of  the  Axis  Totalitarian 

10/17/2016 

Page  835 

Alliance.  We  came  together  as  in  no  other  time  to  win  that  war  and  this  moment  of  Victory  should 
provide  a window  to  our  future  that  every  American  will  understand,  and  to  a time  of  our  greatest 
achievement  as  a Nation  to  this  day  through  our  selfless  sacrifice  and  our  commitment  to  a clear  and 
defining  common  cause.  This  is  the  rallying  moment  than  can  form  the  framework  to  reawaken  American 
Greatness  and  Alignment  based  on  a cause  of  Great  Purpose.  For  any  Nation  to  succeed  it 
must  always  redefine  the  next  clear  objective  for  50  to  100  years  in  todays  accelerating  world  of 
change.  This  vision  must  always  be  reexamined. 

In  the  years  that  followed,  America's  Leadership  was  vital  to  the  rebuilding  of  Europe  and  the  Pacific. 
Under  both  Democratic  and  Republican  Presidents,  the  foundation  for  the  modernization  of  World 
Civilization  in  the  Rebuilding  of  Europe,  Japan  and  the  Pacific  was  laid  with  the  Marshall  Plan  under 
President  Truman.  The  Interstate  Highway  System  was  initiated  under  President  Eisenhower,  and 
President  Kennedy  initiated  the  Apollo  Space  Program.  The  building  of  the  major  infrastructure  projects 
of  the  20  Century  began  in  earnest,  based  on  nonrenewable  and  highly  polluting  resources,  so  there 
was  only  a limited  time  that  we  could  use  them.  In  the  end  many  of  the  chess  moves  between  the  United 
States  and  Soviet  Union  and  various  alliances  and  proxy  wars  that  followed  in  the  last  half  of  the  20th 
Century  were  in  the  Middle  East  primarily  because  of  our  need  for  oil  to  run  our  accelerating  growth  and 
civilization.  Every  move  we  made  to  counter  the  Soviets  has  come  back  to  hurt  us  - Since  9-11  we  have 
continued  to  be  engaged  in  this  continuation  of  war  and  at  every  turn  there  has  been  a new 
manifestation  of  war  like  a cancer. 

Now,  we  must  move  to  unlimited  Clean  Renewable  Resources  to  avert  a repeat  of  the  destruction  and 
major  wars  of  the  20th  Century.  We  have  just  continued  into  this  Century,  15  years  of  continued  War 
with  more  to  follow  with  the  development  of  ISIS.  Climate  Change  will  exacerbate  all  the  problems  of 
population  growth,  poverty  etc.  The  plan  I am  sending  you  addresses  The  Five  Critical  Challenges  of 
the  21  Century:  1.  Population  Growth  and  Cities,  2.  Sustainable  Infrastructure  and  Cities,  3. 

Poverty  and  Economic  Balance,  4.  War  and  Peace,  and  5.  Climate  Change.  Each  of  these  issues  is 
interrelated  as  well  as  converging. 

In  this  presentation  I am  sending  you  is  an  important  strategy  that  will  lift  us  beyond  our  divisions  and 
can  lead  the  Democratic  Party  to  victory  in  the  next  election  so  that  President  Clinton  and  President 
Obama's  important  work  to  bring  us  to  a more  Peaceful  and  Sustainable  World  can  gain  momentum  and 
not  be  stopped  by  fear  and  division.  This  message  is  a key.

GrowGreen  Power  Inc. 

Introduction  - World  Trends  Converge  - The  Fundamentals  of  Food  & Energy 

a 

growgreen  power 

Converging  trends  in  population  growth  and  resource  depletion  have  set  the  stage  for  major  changes  in  our  global  trading  system  as  well 
as  presenting  once-in-a-lifetime  opportunities  in  alternative  energy  and  agriculture.  Our  current  7.3  billion  World  Population  is  growing 
by  approximately  eighty  (80)  million  people  per  year,  and  is  expected  to  reach  10 billion  by  2050.  According  to  the  BBC  - Agriculture 
experts  contend  that  in  order  to  meet  rising  demand,  global  food  production  will  need  to  increase  fifty  (50)  to  seventy  (70)  percent  by 
2050. 

The  fundamentals  of  the  oil  industry  are  inescapable.  The  reality  is,  we  are  not  running  out  of  oil,  but  we  are  "running  out  of  oil  we  can 
offord  to  burn,  and  this  fact  is  going  to  bring  about  major  changes  in  the  way  we  conduct  our  economy."  - Jeff  Rubin.  There  are  steps 
we  can  take  to  minimize  the  potential  impact  of  triple  digit  oil  prices  to  our  economy,  and  address  our  need  to  rapidly  increase  our  food 
production.  In  fact,  it  is  possible  to  capitalize  on  opportunities  developing  from  the  inevitable  rise  in  energy  prices  while  simultaneously 
revitalizing  and  modernizing  our  local  economy  in  America  and  in  cities  around  the  World. 

GrowGreen  Power  Inc. 

GrowGreen  Power  is  the  developer  of  commercial  scale  Hydroponic  Greenhouses  integrated  with  renewable  energy  power  generation 
that  combines  Concentrating  Solar  Thermal  Collectors  and  Biomass  energy  systems.  The  integration  of  the  greenhouse  and  the  energy 
systems  has  created  a unique,  sustainable  and  highly  efficient  local  / food  produce  / renewable  energy  platform  and  business  model. 

One  GrowGreen  Power  Center,  with  a fully  climate  controlled,  Hydroponic  Greenhouse  (100-acre)  will  deliver  an  abundance  of  fresh 
produce  to  the  local  marketplace  in  varieties  that  are  tailored  for  a specific  region.  The  mix  will  typically  include  a variety  of  vegetables  - 
several  kinds  of  tomatoes,  bell  peppers,  cucumbers,  strawberries,  varieties  of  lettuce  and  herbs  - with  annual  production  yields  totaling 
more  than  35,000  metric  tons,  or  more  than  77  million  pounds  / year,  A typical  GrowGreen  Power  Center  is  so  productive  that  a fully 
climate  controlled  GGP  Center,  will  produce  30-X  times  the  yield  of  traditional  agriculture  per  acre,  using  85%  less  water,  in  a pesticide 
free,  clean,  climate  protectected  growing  environment,  while  at  the  same  time  delivering  45-MW  of  clean  renewable  electricity  to  the 
local  power  grid. 

GrowGreen  Power  Centers  are  sustainable  with  the  ability  to  operate  24  hours  a day  365  days  a year  in  most  climate  zones  and  locations 
around  the  world.  This  is  made  possible  by  our  unique  integration  of  technologies  that  include  erecting  a Concentrating  Solar  Thermal 
array  over  the  Greenhouse  - combined  with  a Biomass  Power  Plant.  These  two  systems  of  producing  steam,  when  combined,  drive  steam 
turbines  generating  45  megawatts  of  clean  / renewable  / electricity.  This  capability,  along  with  our  ability  to  maximize  the  reuse  of  the 
thermal  energy  we  collect  to  produce  electricity,  will  also  maintain  our  climate  control  systems  in  a wide  variety  of  climate  zones. 

GGP  - Strategic  Plan  - The  Green  Zone  / Sustainable  Energy  and  Light  Industry  Centers  in  American  Cities 

The  GrowGreen  Power  Inc  Development  Strategy  will  be  to  locate  GGP  Centers  within  50  miles  of  major  Cities  in  the  United  States  as  well 
as  Cities  around  the  World,  and  deliver  both  Sustainable  Fresh  Produce  and  Dean  / Renewable  / Energy  to  the  local  community.  GGP- 
Centers  will  provide  approximately  500  Green  Economy  Jobs  at  every  facility.  We  anticipate  that  with  the  development  of  each  GGP- 
Center  that  there  will  be  subsequent  phases  that  will  eventually  produce  thousands  of  additional  jobs.  In  addition  GGP  Centers  will  be 
the  catalyst  anchor  to  support  the  development  of  local  Green  Economic  Zones  with  Light  Industry  Business  Development  Parks  around 
American  Cities  that  will  bring  many  Light  Industry  manufacturing  jobs  back  to  American  Communities.  These  new  Economic  Green 
Zones  can  now  be  master  planned  in  a far  more  sustainable  configuration  than  has  been  developed  to  date. 

The  collaborative  approach  is  the  key  to  gaining  insight  into  sustainable  solutions  for  the  21s'  Century.  To  this  end  GrowGreen  Power  Inc 
has  secured  strategic  relationships  with  best-in-class  professionals,  and  companies  in  each  of  its  operating  areas.  At  present  GGP  is 
focused  on  developing  our  first  project  50  Miles  from  Charlotte,  North  Carolina.

To:  All  Georgetown  University  Student,  Faculty  and  Staff  Employees 

As  part  of  the  District  of  Columbia  Wage  Theft  Prevention  Act,  all  employers  in  the  District  must  provide  written 
notice  to  all  employees  of  certain  information  regarding  their  pay  and  employment.  The  notice  must  include 
information  about  the  employer,  the  employee's  rate  of  pay,  the  basis  for  that  rate,  and  the  regular  payday. 
Furthermore,  a new  notice  must  be  provided  each  time  that  the  required  information  changes. 

To  comply  with  this  requirement,  Georgetown  University  will  be  sending  notices  to  all  employees  via  GMS. 
Employees  will  receive  notification  of  a pending  action  in  their  GMS  Inbox,  after  which  they  should  review  the 
notice  and  acknowledge  receipt  of  the  notice.  Additional  notices  will  be  sent  each  time  that  changes  are  made  to 
the  required  information. 

The  provision  and  acknowledgement  of  this  notice  is  a statutory  mandate,  and  we  appreciate  your  assistance 
and  cooperation.  Your  first  GMS  notice  will  be  delivered  on  May  18,  2015.

From:  "Gene  Karpinski,  League  of  Conservation  Voters"  <Josh  Hicks@lcv.ora> 
To:  john.podesta@amail.com 
Date:  3/28/2013  5:31:44  AM 
Subject:  Environmental  Majority  Council  Update 

LEAGUE  OF  CONSERVATION  VOTERS 

Dear  John, 

It  has  been  a busy  couple  weeks  in  Washington,  DC,  from  the  all-night  budget  fight  to  President  Obama's  announcement  of  five  new  national 
monuments  which  includes  some  of  the  country's  most  beautiful  wild  places.  LCV  is  on  the  front  lines  of  environmental  protections  and  your 
partnership  as  a member  of  the  Environmental  Majority  Council  is  essential  to  our  success.  Read  on  to  see  some  of  the  most  important  recent 
updates  and  ways  you  can  continue  to  take  action  to  protect  our  planet. 

Thank  you  for  being  a partner  in  this  work. 

Gene 

LCV  Launches  Field  Campaign  to  Elect  Climate  Champion  Ed  Markey 

On  March  1 1 , LCV  announced  the  launch  of  a grassroots  field  campaign  to  help  elect  Ed  Markey  as  the  next  United  States  Senator  from 
Massachusetts.  Since  his  first  election  to  the  U.S.  House  in  1976,  Markey  has  consistently  been  the  one  of  the  strongest  voices  in  the  House  of 
Representatives  on  addressing  climate  change,  protecting  the  environment,  and  promoting  clean  energy.  And  we  need  his  voice  in  the  Senate. 
LCV  will  spend  at  least  $650,000  on  this  field  campaign  by  the  Democratic  Senate  primary  on  April  30th,  knocking  on  at  least  219,000  doors  of 
likely  primary  voters  across  the  state. 

LCV  talked  to  many  of  these  same  voters  during  our  successful  grassroots  campaign  to  elect  Senator  Elizabeth  Warren  last  year.  In  that 
race,  we  spent  more  than  $870,000  on  a field  campaign  to  defeat  then-Senator  Scott  Brown,  and  knocked  on  more  than  400,000  doors  in 
Massachusetts.  LCV  knows  how  to  win  races  and  we're  looking  forward  to  bringing  another  environmental  champion  to  the  Senate. 

To  view  an  example  of  the  literature  we  are  using  for  this  campaign,  please  click  here. 

Stop  the  Dangerous  Keystone  XL  Pipeline! 

This  is  it:  Big  Oil  and  other  dirty  polluters  are  pulling  out  all  the  stops  to  get  the  Keystone  XL  tar  sands  pipeline  built.  They  know  that  a final 
decision  is  expected  this  year  and  they  see  an  opening  to  get  it  done.  But  anyone  who  thinks  that  the  pipeline  won't  have  a devastating  effect 
on  our  climate  has  got  their  heads  in  the  (tar)  sand!  The  pipeline  would  transport  the  dirtiest  oil  on  the  planet  right  through  the  middle  of  our 
country,  resulting  in  far  more  global  warming  pollution  than  conventional  oil  and  threatening  our  precious  waterways  with  disastrous  spills. 

If  we  sit  back,  if  we  don't  take  action  right  now,  this  climate  nightmare  could  be  Big  Oil's  next  big  win  with  devastating  effects.  The  State 
Department  recently  came  out  with  a completely  unacceptable  report  about  the  environmental  impacts  of  the  dangerous  Keystone  XL  tar  sands 
pipeline  and  in  response  the  campaign  to  stop  this  massive  threat  to  our  climate  is  shifting  into  high  gear.  Click  here  to  submit 
your  comment  to  the  Obama  administration  that  they  must  reject  this  dirty  pipeline. 

Big  Votes  on  Climate,  Clean  Air,  and  Keystone  XL  on  the  Senate's  Budget  Resolution 

Last  week,  the  Senate  voted  on  several  high-profile  environmental  issues  during  a late-night  "vote-a-rama"  that  included  close  to  1 00 
amendments  to  Senator  Patty  Murray's  Budget  Resolution,  the  Senate  counterpart  to  the  infamous  Ryan  budget  in  the  House.  While  the  Murray 
budget  does  not  have  the  force  of  law,  the  amendment  votes  were  symbolically  important  as  measures  of  the  Senate's  support  on  some  of  our 
top  priority  issues. 

The  good  news  is  that  a bipartisan  majority  of  Senators  stood  with  the  environment  to  oppose  two  high-profile  amendments:  one,  to  defund 
efforts  by  federal  agencies  to  reduce  carbon  pollution  that  is  causing  climate  change,  failed  53-46  on  a 60  vote  threshold,  and  another,  which 
sought  to  weaken  the  EPA's  landmark  Mercury  and  Air  Toxics  Standards,  the  first  ever  national  limits  on  toxic  mercury  pollution  from  power 
plants,  failed  on  a 46-53  vote.  These  strong  votes  to  defeat  these  amendments  underscore  support  for  the  EPA's  work  protecting  public  health 
and  holding  polluters  accountable. 

The  bad  news  is  that  Big  Oil  bought  itself  a meaningless  victory  on  an  amendment,  which  passed  62-37,  supporting  approval  and  construction 
of  the  dangerous  Keystone  XL  tar  sands  pipeline.  This  amendment  doesn't  change  the  fact  that  the  ultimate  decision  remains  with  President 
Obama.  But  we  must  hold  Senators  accountable  for  siding  with  Big  Oil,  especially  those  otherwise  pro-environment  Senators  who  flip-flopped 
on  this  issue  since  it  came  up  for  a vote  last  year.  Stay  tuned  for  more  on  LCV's  accountability  efforts. 

GREAT  NEWS:  Shell  Won't  Drill  in  the  Arctic! 

Shell  Oil  Company  just  announced  earlier  this  month  that  they  will  not  drill  in  the  Arctic  Ocean  in  2013.  To  date  almost  92,000  LCV  members  have 
signed  our  petition  to  get  Shell  out  of  the  Arctic.  And  now,  in  the  face  of  so  much  grassroots  pressure,  they  have  decided  that  they  won't  move 
forward  with  their  irresponsible  project  this  year. 

10/17/2016

But  this  good  news  comes  with  a caveat.  Shell  promises  to  "pause"  drilling  this  year,  not  shut  it  down  altogether.  If  we  want  Shell  to  keep  its 
dirty  rigs  and  unsafe  equipment  out  of  our  pristine  Arctic  waters,  we  need  our  government  to  take  a stand  against  Arctic  drilling. 

With  your  help,  we  can  keep  the  momentum  going  and  win  this  campaign.  Will  you  join  us  in  calling  on  the  Obama  administration  to  oppose 
Shell's  dangerous  Arctic  drilling  plans? 

LCV  & State  LCVs  Annual  Conference  in  May 

Please  join  me  for  LCV  and  State  LCVs  Annual  Conference,  which  will  be  held  on  May  2-4,  2013  in  Grand  Rapids,  Michigan.  This  year  we  will 
also  be  convening  a special  Partners  in  Conservation  event  on  May  3rd.  This  will  offer  a unique  opportunity  for  members  of  the  environmental 
funding  community  from  across  the  country  to  collaborate,  learn,  and  strategize  with  the  members  of  the  state  league  movement.  We  are  at  a 
crossroads.  We  can  either  rebuild  power  to  solve  the  greatest  environmental  challenges  before  us,  or  we  can  allow  special  interests  to  gut 
longstanding  environmental  regulations  and  foster  inaction  on  the  climate  crisis.  The  next  generation  is  counting  on  us  to  safeguard  our  planet. 
With  your  partnership,  we  will  succeed. 

For  more  information  on  Partners  in  Conservation  and  the  Annual  Conference,  please  contact  Will  Roberts  at  (206)  631-2639  or 
Will  Roberts@lcv.ora  . You  won't  want  to  miss  this  chance  to  shape  the  future  of  the  environmental  movement. 

GiveGreerr.  Because  Not  All  Money  is  "Green" 

To  date,  LCV  Action  Fund  has  now  raised  and  contributed  over  $214,000  in  support  of  our  priority  candidates  this  cycle.  For  environmental 
supporters  like  yourself,  the  best  giving  strategy  is  to  "bundle"  your  contributions  with  contributions  from  others  who  share  your  environmental 
values.  Bundling  through  LCV  Action  Fund's  GiveGreen  website  magnifies  the  power  of  your  contribution  by  calling  attention  to  the 
environmental  values  that  drive  you  to  support  the  candidate  in  the  first  place.  Please  visit  www.aiveareen.com  today  to  support  LCV  Action 
Fund's  featured  environmental  champions.

TODAY'S  TABLE  OF  CONTENTS 

SEN.  CLINTON'S  CAMPAIGN: 

+ Clinton  Makes  Case  For  Continuing  Campaign. 

+ Clinton:  VP  Speculation  Premature. 

+ Chelsea  Clinton,  Michelle  Obama  Campaign  In  Puerto  Rico. 

+ Edwards  Endorses  Obama. 

+ Clinton  Campaign  Surprised  By  NARAL's  Endorsement  Of  Obama. 

+ Obama  Reaches  Out  To  White  Blue  Collar  Voters. 

+ Obama  Apologies  For  Calling  Reporter  "Sweetie." 

Sen.  Clinton's  Campaign: 

CLINTON  MAKES  CASE  FOR  CONTINUING  CAMPAIGN.  In  the  wake  of  her  lopsided  West  Virginia  primary  win 
on  Tuesday,  Sen.  Hillary  Clinton  vowed  to  press  ahead  with  her  presidential  campaign  despite  the  conventional 
wisdom  that  her  rival,  Barack  Obama,  has  all  but  secured  the  nomination.  Clinton  herself  did  a round  of  TV 
interviews  to  justify  her  continued  campaign,  and  she  dispatch  key  surrogates  to  meet  with  congressional 
supporters  and  undecided  superdelegates. 

The  AP  (5/15,  Fouhy)  reports  Hillary  Clinton  "vowed  to  remain  in  the  presidential  race  until  the  final  primaries 
next  month  while  her  campaign  built  a case  that  she  now  leads  in  the  popular  vote  if  the  disputed  contests  in 
Michigan  and  Florida  are  counted."  Clinton  "gave  a round  of  television  interviews  Wednesday  before  meeting 
with  her  finance  team  and  top  fundraisers  at  her  Washington  home."  Participants  "described  the  session  as 
upbeat  and  said  the  unifying  message  was  that  Clinton,  with  her  lopsided  victory  over  front-runner  Barack 
Obama  in  West  Virginia  on  Tuesday,  now  had  the  lead  in  votes  cast  thus  far.  The  numbers,  however,  include  the 
results  from  the  Florida  and  Michigan  primaries,  which  the  national  Democratic  Party  has  not  recognized." 

Clinton  Tells  Capitol  Hill  Supporters  She  Is  Staying  In  Race.  The  Hill  (5/15,  Bolton)  reports  Clinton  "rallied  her 
Capitol  Hill  supporters  on  Wednesday  night,  telling  them  to  bring  an  uncommitted  friend  and  seeking  to  capitalize 
on  her  41 -percentage  points  victory  in  the  West  Virginia  primary."  Although  the  endorsement  of  John  Edwards 
"handed  Obama  the  support  of  a candidate  whose  appeal  was  largely  to  blue-collar  workers,  Clinton  used  the 
meeting  at  the  Sewell-Belmont  House  to  drive  home  the  point  that  she  is  more  competitive  with  precisely  that 
category  of  voter,  and  in  districts  where  Democrats  will  face  their  toughest  races  this  fall."  Clinton's  senior 
campaign  adviser,  Harold  Ickes,  "met  her  congressional  whip  team  Wednesday  morning  to  make  clear  that  she 
intends  to  stay  in  the  race  until  June  3,  the  date  of  the  last  primary,  despite  recent  speculation  that  she  might 
drop  her  bid  after  Oregon  and  Kentucky  hold  primaries  on  May  20." 

CLINTON:  VP  SPECULATION  PREMATURE.  Asked  about  the  vice  presidency  on  CNN's  The  Situation  Room  (5/ 
14,  Blitzer),  Sen.  Hillary  Clinton  said,  "It's  premature  for  either  of  us  to  talk  about  that.  I think  both  of  us  are 
committed  to  doing  everything  we  can  to  win  in  the  fall.  I certainly  am.  And  I will  do  whatever  it  takes,  because  I 
know  what  four  more  years  of  basically  the  same  Bush  policies  would  mean  to  America." 

NBC  Nightly  News  (5/14,  story  2,  4:25,  Williams,  9.87M)  interviewed  Sen.  Clinton.  Asked  about  the  "argument  that 
you  and  Senator  Obama  are  better  together,"  Clinton  said,  "Well,  I know  a lot  of  people  are  making  that 
argument.  I am  not  entertaining  it  yet  because  I'm  still  focused  on  getting  the  nomination,  but  I know  that  once  we 
have  a nominee,  we're  going  to  have  a unified  Democratic  Party."

Rendell  Pushes  For  Clinton  Obama  Alliance.  The  Pittsburgh  Tribune-Review  (5/15)  reports,  "Gov.  Ed  Rendell 
- one  of  Hillary  Clinton's  most  vocal  supporters  - told  CNN  on  Wednesday  that  Barack  Obama  should  choose 
Clinton  as  his  running  mate  if  Obama  becomes  the  Democratic  nominee  for  president."  Rendell  said  "I  don't  know 
whether  she  would  accept.  I don't  know  whether  he  would  do  it,"  but  "you've  got  the  real  thing"  with  Clinton, 
"someone  who  has  energized  voters." 

CHELSEA  CLINTON,  MICHELLE  OBAMA  CAMPAIGN  IN  PUERTO  RICO.  The  Miami  Herald  (5/15,  Mcfadden, 
253K)  reports,  "Two  prominent  surrogates  of  Barack  Obama  and  Hillary  Rodham  Clinton  stumped  for  the 
candidates  Wednesday,  a sign  of  how  important  this  U.S.  island  territory's  primary  next  month  has  become. 
Michelle  Obama  toured  the  capital  of  San  Juan  for  her  husband,  who  remains  in  a marathon  fight  for  the 
Democratic  presidential  nomination.  Her  first  visit  to  the  island  coincided  with  Chelsea  Clinton's  second  trip  here 
to  pitch  her  mother's  candidacy."  The  Herald  adds,  "Meanwhile,  the  U.S.  Navy  denied  Chelsea  Clinton 
permission  to  campaign  on  a former  bombing  range  on  the  outlying  island  of  Vieques.  The  range  was  closed  in 
April  2003  after  years  of  protests  over  two  errant  bombs  that  killed  a security  guard.  Hillary  Clinton's  campaign 
wanted  to  use  the  site  as  a setting  to  discuss  her  plan  to  clean  up  the  land  and  give  some  of  it  to  residents.  But 
Navy  spokeswoman  Lt.  Lara  Bollinger  said  no  one  is  allowed  to  campaign  on  federal  property." 

EDWARDS  ENDORSES  OBAMA.  John  Edwards'  endorsement  of  Barack  Obama  is  being  treated  as  a major 
development  by  the  media,  leading  all  three  network  newscasts  and  figuring  prominently  on  the  front  pages  of 
major  newspapers.  The  coverage  portrays  Edwards'  endorsement  as  an  indication  the  Democratic  establishment 
is  lining  up  behind  Obama,  but  its  timing  also  is  seen  as  a strategic  move  by  Obama  to  address  his  poor 
performance  among  working-class  white  voters  in  West  Virginia.  ABC  World  News  (5/14,  lead  story,  0:35, 

Gibson,  8.78M)  led  its  report  with  "a  live  picture. ..from  Grand  Rapids,  Michigan,  a Barack  Obama  campaign  rally, 
where  John  Edwards  is  about  to  take  stage  and  endorse  Barack  Obama.  ...  His  is  a major  endorsement  sought 
by  both  Obama  and  Hillary  Clinton."  In  a follow-up  report,  ABC  World  News  (5/14,  story  4,  3:10,  Wright,  8.78M) 
added  that  in  West  Virginia,  Obama  "struggled,  in  particular,  among  white,  working-class  voters.  And  those  are 
exactly  the  voters  who  are  the  most  ardent  supporters  of  John  Edwards.  John  Edwards  cast  himself  as  the  angry, 
white  man  of  the  Democratic  primaries.  Now,  he'll  put  that  anger  to  use  for  his  former  rival." 

Later  on  ABC  World  News  (5/14,  story  5,  3:20,  Gibson,  8.78M),  George  Stephanopoulos  said  of  the  Obama 
team,  "They've  been  very  good  at  pulling  out  endorsements  like  this  after  losses.  But  they've  been  working  on 
John  Edwards  for  weeks."  The  Obama  campaign  "said  this  was  Edwards'  decision  to  come  out  now.  He  wanted  to 
come  out  when  he  thought  the  race  was  over,  when  he  could  also  have  the  maximum  impact." 

NBC  Nightly  News  (5/14,  lead  story,  2:05,  Williams,  9.87M)  refers  to  a "major  boost"  for  Obama,  and  notes 
Edwards  "got  seven  percent  of  the  vote  last  night  in  West  Virginia.  Interesting  because  he's  not  in  the  running 
anymore.  But  it  does  show  support  for  him  still  out  there."  And  the  CBS  Evening  News  (5/14,  lead  story,  3:00, 
Couric,  7.66M)  reported,  "Clinton  didn't  get  to  enjoy  her  landslide  win  in  West  Virginia  very  long  at  all.  Barack 
Obama  took  back  the  spotlight  this  evening  dramatically  when  he  won  an  endorsement  both  candidates  wanted 
badly  John  Edwards."  CBS  (Reynolds)  added,  "The  picture  of  these  candidates  out  here,  the  former  candidate 
and  the  current  candidate  on  stage  together  tonight  will  be  almost  irresistible  for  those  in  search  of  party  unity. 

So  this  is  a very  well-timed  announcement  on  a number  of  levels."  Edwards'  "1 1th  hour  timing  may  well  be 
designed  as  a signal  to  remaining  superdelegates  that  the  time  to  make  up  their  minds  has  come  and  that  the 
party  should  coalesce  around  Obama." 

The  AP  (5/15,  Babington)  reports  Edwards  "made  the  carefully  timed  announcement  at  an  Obama  rally,"  and 
"received  a thunderous  ovation  when  Obama  introduced  him  to  the  crowd  of  several  thousand."  Said  Edwards, 
"Brothers  and  sisters,  we  must  come  together  as  Democrats"  to  defeat  McCain.  He  added,  "We  are  here  tonight 
because  the  Democratic  voters  have  made  their  choice,  and  so  have  I." 

The  New  York  Times  (5/15,  A1 , Sullivan,  Bosman,  1 .18M)  notes  Edwards  "went  on  to  say,  'There  is  one  man  who 
knows  in  his  heart  that  it  is  time  to  tear  down  that  wall  and  make  one  America,  Barack  Obama.'"  Obama  "noted 
how  Mr.  Edwards  and  his  wife,  Elizabeth,  had  emphasized  health  care  as  an  issue  that  is  of  primary  concern, 
then  said  it  would  be  a major  issue  in  his  administration."  The  endorsement  "comes  at  a time  when  the  appeal  of 
Mr.  Obama  appears  to  be  lagging  among  white,  blue-collar  voters,  a group  to  which  Mr.  Edwards  openly 
appealed." 

CLINTON  CAMPAIGN  SURPRISED  BY  NARAL'S  ENDORSEMENT  OF  OBAMA.  McClatchv  (5/15,  Talev)  reports 
John  Edwards'  endorsement  "came  hours  after  abortion-rights  group  NARAL  deserted  Clinton  after  years  of 
support  to  endorse  Obama."  These  "joint  endorsements  suggest  that  despite  Clinton's  big  victory  Tuesday  and 
her  determination  to  keep  fighting  for  the  nomination,  important  parts  of  the  Democratic  Party  are  jumping 
aboard  the  Obama  bandwagon  before  they're  left  behind."  The  Clinton  campaign  "was  caught  unawares  by  the 

10/17/2016
